function Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Counts the devices that signed in recently and are marked compliant, for the devices-compliant measure.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The reader of the devices-compliant measure (powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1), which decides the step
    intune.devices-compliant of the defender's path. A Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant device
    blocks every device that Microsoft Entra ID doesn't mark compliant, so the share of compliant devices among the
    devices in use says whether such a policy can be turned on.

    Reads the enabled devices in Microsoft Entra ID that signed in within the last SignedInWithinDays days
    (approximateLastSignInDateTime), through the Graph cache. A device counts when isCompliant is true: Intune or
    an approved MDM sets it, and it is what a compliant-device grant checks. Devices that are not compliant are
    returned as the objects that fall short, most recent sign-in first, whether they are managed (isManaged) and
    noncompliant or not managed at all.

    A device that has no Microsoft Entra identity (neither registered nor joined) can't be seen this way, so it is
    neither counted nor listed. A compliant-device policy blocks it too.

    Returns an object with Count (compliant devices), Total (devices that signed in) and Objects (the devices that
    aren't compliant, as Type, Id and DisplayName).

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare

    Returns the number of compliant devices among the enabled devices that signed in within the last 30 days.

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare -SignedInWithinDays 14

    Counts only the devices that signed in within the last 14 days.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        # Devices that signed in within this many days are counted. approximateLastSignInDateTime is approximate, so
        # keep it well above a week.
        [ValidateRange(1, 365)]
        [int] $SignedInWithinDays = 30
    )

    # Start of the UTC day, so the request, and so its cache entry, stays the same for the whole day.
    $since = [datetime]::UtcNow.Date.AddDays(-$SignedInWithinDays).ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ', [cultureinfo]::InvariantCulture)
    $deviceSplat = @{
        RelativeUri     = 'devices'
        Filter          = "accountEnabled eq true and approximateLastSignInDateTime ge $since"
        # isManaged, operatingSystem and trustType are read for the object facts device.managed, device.os and
        # device.joinType (design section 12), which this reader writes once Add-MtAffectedObjectFact takes a Key.
        Select          = 'id', 'displayName', 'approximateLastSignInDateTime', 'isCompliant', 'isManaged', 'operatingSystem', 'trustType'
        QueryParameters = @{ '$count' = 'true' }
    }
    $devices = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest @deviceSplat | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ })

    $notCompliant = @($devices | Where-Object { $_.isCompliant -ne $true })

    [pscustomobject][ordered]@{
        Count   = $devices.Count - $notCompliant.Count
        Total   = $devices.Count
        Objects = @(
            $notCompliant |
                Sort-Object -Property @{ Expression = { [string]$_.approximateLastSignInDateTime }; Descending = $true }, displayName, id |
                ForEach-Object {
                    [pscustomobject][ordered]@{
                        Type        = 'Device'
                        Id          = [string]$_.id
                        DisplayName = [string]$_.displayName
                    }
                }
        )
    }
}

function Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns Entra directory role assignments, active and PIM-eligible.
    .DESCRIPTION
    Reads directory role assignments the same way for every caller, so the decision of when the PIM
    APIs can be used is made in one place.
    With Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Governance, active assignments come from
    roleAssignmentScheduleInstances, filtered to assignmentType 'Assigned' so an eligible role that is
    temporarily activated is not also returned as active, and eligible assignments come from
    roleEligibilityScheduleInstances. Without those licenses, or when the PIM APIs reject the tenant
    license even though subscribedSkus reports a P2 service plan, active assignments come from
    roleAssignments and eligible assignments are not read.
    Each assignment gets an AssignmentType property of Active or Eligible. The result has two
    properties: Assignments, and EligibleChecked, which is true when eligible assignments were read.
    .EXAMPLE
    $roleAssignments = Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment
    $roleAssignments.Assignments | Where-Object AssignmentType -eq 'Eligible'
    Returns the PIM-eligible assignments of every directory role.
    .EXAMPLE
    (Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -RoleId '62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10' -ExpandPrincipal).Assignments.principal
    Returns the principals that are assigned, or eligible for, the Global Administrator role.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]

function Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns Entra directory role assignments, active and PIM-eligible.
    .DESCRIPTION
    Reads directory role assignments the same way for every caller, so the decision of when the PIM
    APIs can be used is made in one place.
    With Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Governance, active assignments come from
    roleAssignmentScheduleInstances, filtered to assignmentType 'Assigned' so an eligible role that is
    temporarily activated is not also returned as active, and eligible assignments come from
    roleEligibilityScheduleInstances. Without those licenses, or when the PIM APIs reject the tenant
    license even though subscribedSkus reports a P2 service plan, active assignments come from
    roleAssignments and eligible assignments are not read.
    Each assignment gets an AssignmentType property of Active or Eligible. The result has two
    properties: Assignments, and EligibleChecked, which is true when eligible assignments were read.
    .EXAMPLE
    $roleAssignments = Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment
    $roleAssignments.Assignments | Where-Object AssignmentType -eq 'Eligible'
    Returns the PIM-eligible assignments of every directory role.
    .EXAMPLE
    (Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -RoleId '62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10' -ExpandPrincipal).Assignments.principal
    Returns the principals that are assigned, or eligible for, the Global Administrator role.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
19:    $active = $MemberStatus -ne 'Eligible'
24:    $pim = (Get-MtLicenseInformation -Product EntraID) -in @('P2', 'Governance')
37:                    foreach ($assignment in Get-Assignment -Uri 'roleManagement/directory/roleEligibilityScheduleInstances' -Filter $roleFilter -AssignmentType Eligible -Expand $ExpandPrincipal -Property $Select -NoCache $DisableCache) {
42:        } catch {
43:            # subscribedSkus can report a P2 service plan that the PIM APIs do not accept
45:                Write-Verbose 'PIM APIs require Entra ID P2 or Governance in this tenant. Using role assignments instead.'
55:        # Free or P1 tenant (PIM APIs cannot be called on non-P2 tenants)
65:        EligibleChecked = $eligible -and $pim

@{
    Measures = @(
        @{
            # Step intune.devices-compliant. No License: isCompliant can also come from an approved third-party MDM,
            # and in a tenant without one the figure (no device is compliant) is what the step needs to show.
            Key        = 'devices-compliant'
            Function   = 'Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare'
            Title      = 'Devices that sign in are compliant'
            Unit       = 'devices'
            Service    = 'Graph'
            Permission = 'Graph:Scope:Device.Read.All | Graph:Scope:Directory.Read.All'
        }
        @{
            # Step entra.mfa-registered. The registration report needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 and AuditLog.Read.All.
            Key        = 'mfa-registered'
            Function   = 'Get-MtMfaRegistrationShare'
            Title      = 'Enabled member users are registered for MFA'
            Unit       = 'users'
            Service    = 'Graph'
            License    = 'AAD_PREMIUM'
            Permission = ('Graph:Scope:AuditLog.Read.All', 'Graph:Scope:Directory.Read.All')
        }
    )
}

# M5 measures: hand-over notes (session defenders-path-m5, branch claude/defenders-path-m5-0f5456)

Written 2026-11-05. Based on local feat/defenders-path at 39c31c9f6 ("make readiness a measure on the step").
No MT tests and no MT ID reservation: the owner ruled readiness is a measure, not a test.

## What the branch adds

- `powershell/internal/services/entra/Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare.ps1`: reads `devices` with
  `accountEnabled eq true and approximateLastSignInDateTime ge <start of UTC day minus 30 days>` (`$count=true`,
  through the cache). Count = `isCompliant` true; Objects = the rest, newest sign-in first. Optional
  `-SignedInWithinDays` (default 30).
- `powershell/internal/services/entra/Get-MtMfaRegistrationShare.ps1`: reads the whole
  `reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails` (no select, so the cache entry can be shared) and
  `users?$filter=accountEnabled eq false`. Counts `userType` member, `isMfaRegistered` true. Leaves out disabled
  users, `Get-MtEmergencyAccessAccount` users and the user members of its groups (recursive), and user members of
  the DirectorySynchronizationAccounts / OnPremisesDirectorySyncAccount roles. Objects = unregistered users,
  admins first.
- `powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1`: entries `devices-compliant` (no License, see below) and
  `mfa-registered` (License AAD_PREMIUM, AuditLog.Read.All).
- `powershell/tests/functions/MeasureReaders.Tests.ps1`.

## For whoever merges M2 and M5

Steps files were not touched. Add to the catalogue, and delete each step's `Unchecked` line:

- `intune.devices-compliant`: `"Measure": { "Key": "devices-compliant", "MinimumShare": 95 }`
- `entra.mfa-registered`: `"Measure": { "Key": "mfa-registered", "MinimumShare": 95 }`

## Open points for the design owner

- The design's registry example gives `devices-compliant` `License = 'INTUNE_A'`. Left out: an approved
  third-party MDM can set isCompliant on Windows, and in a tenant without Intune "0 of N compliant" is the figure
  the step should show, not Unknown.
- "Devices with no Entra identity can't be seen, and the result says so": the reader's contract (Count, Total,
  Objects) and the registry keys have no field for a note. M3/M4 need one (a registry `Note`, or text in the
  report) to say it.
- Object facts: maester365/maester#2681 merged into main at 2026-11-05T04:21Z, after feat/defenders-path
  branched, so `Add-MtAffectedObjectFact` isn't on this branch. Once it is, the readers call it on the listed
  objects: devices `device.compliant`, `device.managed`, `device.os` (operatingSystem), `device.joinType`
  (trustType); users `user.mfaRegistered`, under the object ID and the UPN. The device reader already selects
  those fields.
- isMfaRegistered vs isMfaCapable: the brief and fact key say registered. isMfaCapable also requires the method
  to be allowed by the authentication methods policy, so it is the stricter "can complete MFA" figure
  (CIS.M365.5.2.3.4 uses it).

git worktree remove --force /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill-github-maester--claude-worktrees-defenders-path-m5-0f5456/cfe982e3-684a-4f53-a9be-613b4c761f4f/scratchpad/base && git status --short && git add powershell/internal/services/entra/Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare.ps1 powershell/internal/services/entra/Get-MtMfaRegistrationShare.ps1 powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1 powershell/tests/functions/MeasureReaders.Tests.ps1 && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(engine): add the devices-compliant and mfa-registered measures

The two readers of the defender's path measures (design section 11), with
their entries in the measure registry.

- Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare reads the enabled Entra devices that signed in
  within 30 days and counts those with isCompliant. The devices that are not
  compliant, the ones a compliant-device policy would block, are the objects.
  No License in the registry: an approved third-party MDM can set isCompliant.
- Get-MtMfaRegistrationShare reads the whole registration report and counts
  the member users with isMfaRegistered. It leaves out disabled users, the
  configured emergency access accounts and the users in their groups, and the
  directory synchronization accounts. Needs Entra ID P1.

The catalogue's Measure entries for intune.devices-compliant and
entra.mfa-registered are left to the merge with the M2 catalogue branch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -3; git status --short
